extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and classification of the basic data of philosophy: the epistemic status of consciousness, the criterion of knowledge as congruity between representations and presentations, and the distinction between two orders of mental manifestations (vivid vs faint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge as congruity between representations and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge consists in the consciousness of a definite set of impressions standing in definite relations disclosed under definite conditions; when present experience (presentations) perfectly corresponds with represented impressions (ideas, anticipations) from past experience, the cognition attains its highest certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: identifying gold by correspondence of weight, lack of reaction to nitric acid, malleability, fusion point, crystallization, etc. The more matches between anticipated (ideal) effects and actual (real) effects, the stronger the justification for asserting knowledge. Generalization/hypotheses are verified when entire congruity is found between the states of consciousness constituting them and those given in perception or reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy's justificatory task: show congruity with all dicta of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy must justify its fundamental assumptions by showing their congruity with all other dicta (deliverances) of consciousness; proving or disproving congruity is the business of philosophy and the complete establishment of congruity equals the unification of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy aims for a complete unification of knowledge by demonstrating that an ultimate proposition is congruous with the whole range of experience. The process of testing a fundamental assumption consists in showing its agreement with all other conscious deliverances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of accepting consciousness' verdict (likeness/unlikeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: We must accept as true the verdict of consciousness that some manifestations are like one another and some are unlike; this primordial act is unavoidable because reasoning presupposes that consciousness can judge likeness and difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careless comparisons can be revised by more careful comparison; the revised, deliberate verdict is preferable. The permanence (survival) of a consciousness of likeness or difference under critical examination is the ultimate warrant for asserting that likeness or difference exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy requires a substantive ultimate datum coextensive with experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond assuming the trustworthiness of consciousness as a process, philosophy must accept as unquestionable at least one fundamental deliverance (a substantive proposition) of consciousness that is as general as possible and co-extensive with all experience; this proposition must specify the widest and most profound distinction present in experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ultimate principle intended to unify all experience must express a piece of knowledge (not merely the validity of an act of knowing) and must specify the antithesis between two ultimate classes of experiences in which all others merge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness: vivid manifestations vs faint manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: One order of manifestations is vivid (more distinct, as in perception) and the other is faint (less distinct, as in reflection, memory, imagination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vivid manifestations (perceptual impressions) are usually unmistakably distinct from faint ones (ideas); rare borderline cases (e.g. near darkness or pathology) exist but are exceptions. Vivid typically precede the faint historically (idea as a feeble repetition of the original impression). Examples: perceptual sight/sound vs recollection/idea of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals vs copies: vivid are originals, faint are representations/copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid manifestations are originals (presented), while faint manifestations are copies or represented forms (ideas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures the dependence relation: faint manifestations are often produced after and by reference to prior vivid ones, and in many cases would not exist without prior vivid manifestations (though some faint may precede vivid in creative/inventive cases, these do not parallel the natural sequence of idea after impression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity: each order forms a continuous series (no directly known breaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both vivid and faint manifestations form heterogeneous streams or currents that run side by side; each preserves continuity so that no direct breakage of either series is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The currents may ebb and flow in dominance, but both maintain longitudinal continuity; sleep is the only state where vivid manifestations cease to be distinguishable as such and faint ones may be mistaken for them (with awareness restored upon waking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion within orders: vivid manifestions cohere indissolubly; faint cohere loosely
rubrics_metrics.description: Components of the vivid series are bound together both longitudinally and transversely in large, often indissoluble groups; components of the faint series also cohere but their cohesions are mostly dissoluble and rearrangeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: within perception, color, shade, outline cohere as an object and cannot be separated while present; in faint representations one can separate features (e.g., shape vs color in imagination). Only certain generic forms among faint manifestations show stronger cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak inter-series coherence: vivid and faint currents have limited coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Although components of each current cohere among themselves, the vivid and faint currents have relatively little coherence with one another; the vivid is largely unmodifiable by the faint and the faint can become substantially independent of the vivid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically, vivid presentations (landscape, sounds, movements) are uninfluenced by accompanying ideas; the faint current is often perturbed or carried with the vivid (memories, interpretations), but can also flow separately (reverie, reasoning), and occasionally predominate (absence of mind).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions-belong-to-order: conditions of occurrence are of the same order
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions under which manifestations of either order occur themselves belong to that same order; for the faint order the essential antecedent conditions lie among faint manifestations, while for many vivid manifestations the antecedent conditions are not present among concurrent manifestations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: visual qualities presuppose open eyes, yet opening the eyes is itself a vivid manifestation; many vivid changes follow other vivid manifestations or have antecedents outside the stream (flash of lightning, sudden sounds). Emotions and muscular tensions are peculiar vivid cases that can be produced by faint ideas but are classed specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedents and control: faint manifestations have traceable antecedents and are controllable; vivid often arise spontaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Faint manifestations have traceable antecedents, can be produced or suppressed by establishing their conditions; vivid manifestations frequently occur without previous presentation of their antecedents and may persist or cease under unknown or uncontrollable conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ideas can be called up or suppressed by appropriate conditions among thoughts; a flash of lightning or an unexpected crash arises as a vivid manifestation without antecedent in the stream of ideas and cannot be directly affected by current thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence (survival) under critical examination as warrant
rubrics_metrics.description: The permanence or survival of a consciousness of likeness or difference through deliberate, critical examination is the ultimate warrant for asserting existence (likeness/unlikeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rash or casual verdict may be overturned by careful comparison; only those perceptions/identifications that survive critical scrutiny are to be accepted as true. This survival itself is the act of acceptance.
